ideas.name: ImpactIQ
ideas.niche: Quantitative striking performance and load management for combat athletes.
ideas.problem: Combat athletes lack objective, granular data on striking power, velocity, and cumulative impact volume, making it difficult to measure technical progress or detect overtraining before injuries occur.
ideas.targetUser: Competitive amateur and professional combat athletes (Boxing, Muay Thai, MMA) aged 18-40 who utilize wearable technology and prioritize data-driven performance optimization.
coreFeatures: Real-time Velocity & Force Dashboard
Cumulative Fatigue & Injury Risk Scoring
Technique Consistency & Strike Pattern Analysis
Longitudinal Power & Speed Progression Tracking
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) API for sensor communication
High-frequency IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) data processing
Cloud-based time-series database (e.g., InfluxDB or AWS Timestream)
HealthKit/Google Fit API for biometric correlation
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will bypass actual hardware via a MockSensorProvider class that emits a stream of JSON objects every 50ms. To simulate realistic striking, the data will use a base sine wave to represent movement, with sharp, randomized spikes in the 'force' and 'velocity' fields to mimic impact events. Bluetooth pairing will be simulated with a 2.5-second 'Connecting...' delay followed by a success state. Historical data requests will pull from a local JSON file using a 600ms artificial delay to mimic network latency, ensuring the UI shows loading states for realism.

ideas.name: LoadLogic
ideas.niche: Home EV Load Management & Preventative Breaker Protection
ideas.problem: Unmanaged simultaneous high-power draws—such as EV charging occurring alongside HVAC, ovens, or dryers—exceeding the home's electrical capacity and causing circuit breaker trips.
ideas.targetUser: Homeowners with electric vehicles, particularly those in older residences or single-phase electrical setups, who need to maximize charging speed without risking power interruptions.
coreFeatures: Real-time Live Load Dashboard (Amperage/Voltage visualization)
Dynamic Charging Throttling (Automated reduction of EV draw during appliance spikes)
Predictive Trip Alerts (Push notifications when load approaches breaker threshold)
Appliance Signature Detection (AI-driven identification of high-draw devices)
Smart Scheduling (Optimizing charge cycles for off-peak/low-load windows)
realDependencies: Hardware Manufacturer IoT API (Smart Current Clamp telemetry)
OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) or manufacturer-specific EVSE APIs
Smart Home Integration Protocols (Matter, Home Assistant, or Google Home)
Real-time cloud messaging service (AWS IoT Core or Firebase Realtime Database)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will implement a local WebSocket server that emits a continuous JSON stream of telemetry data. This stream will simulate three distinct data tracks: 'Home Base Load' (stable noise), 'Appliance Spikes' (sudden, high-amplitude jumps triggered by virtual buttons), and 'EV Current' (a controllable variable). To simulate real hardware behavior, the emulator will introduce a randomized 500ms–1500ms latency on all command responses and simulate 'packet loss' by occasionally dropping telemetry frames. A 'Scenario Controller' will allow the developer to trigger 'Danger Zone' states where the simulated EV draw exceeds a set threshold, demonstrating the UI's automated throttling response.

ideas.name: AuraLeaf
ideas.niche: Precision environmental management for luxury cigar collections
ideas.problem: Catastrophic loss of high-value cigar investments due to undetected humidity drops, temperature spikes, or sensor malfunctions
ideas.targetUser: Affluent cigar enthusiasts and luxury lounge owners managing investment-grade collections valued in the tens of thousands of dollars
coreFeatures: Real-time environmental telemetry dashboard (Temp, RH, and CO2)
Customizable threshold alerts via push notifications and SMS
Digital cellar log for collection inventory and aging tracking
Smart climate control integration for automated humidity adjustment
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) or Wi-Fi IoT connectivity protocols
Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for real-time alerts
MQTT broker for low-latency sensor data transmission
Time-series database (e.g., InfluxDB) for historical trend logging
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a MockSensorEngine that generates data using a controlled random walk algorithm to simulate realistic, non-linear fluctuations in temperature and humidity. To simulate connectivity, a 'Syncing' state will trigger a 2-second artificial latency using Promises. A 'Simulate Failure' toggle will be provided to force the mock data into critical ranges (e.g., <60% RH), which will trigger a local notification event. The inventory system will be populated with a static JSON manifest of premium brands (e.g., Padrón, Davidoff) to simulate a populated collection.

ideas.name: GlowTrace
ideas.niche: Precision health and stability monitoring for high-end vacuum tube audio hardware
ideas.problem: Vacuum tubes are susceptible to thermal drift and voltage fluctuations that cause inconsistent sonic performance and can lead to catastrophic, expensive component failure if left unmonitored.
ideas.targetUser: High-net-worth audiophiles and boutique hi-fi collectors (ages 35-65) who own high-voltage single-ended or push-pull amplifiers and prioritize both equipment longevity and sonic perfection.
coreFeatures: Live Telemetry Dashboard: Real-time visualization of IR temperature gradients and B+ voltage levels via high-frequency graphing.
Thermal Stabilization Timer: An automated countdown and notification system that alerts the user when the tubes have reached their optimal operating temperature for peak sound quality.
Predictive Health Analytics: AI-driven trend analysis that identifies micro-fluctuations in voltage, signaling potential tube aging or capacitor degradation before failure occurs.
Sonic Sweet-Spot Mapping: A feature that allows users to log their perceived sound quality against current thermal/voltage profiles to find the perfect equilibrium.
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) stack for hardware communication
MQTT or WebSockets for real-time telemetry data streaming
Time-series database (e.g., InfluxDB) for long-term telemetry storage
Firebase Cloud Messaging for critical hardware failure alerts
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'Simulated Hardware Engine' that replaces the BLE stack. This engine will use a state machine to transition through three phases: 'Cold Start' (rapidly rising temperature and fluctuating voltage), 'Steady State' (stable sine-wave jitter around a target temperature/voltage), and 'Anomaly Event' (a sudden simulated voltage spike or thermal runaway). All data will be fed through a local WebSocket emulator with an artificial 150ms jitter to mimic wireless packet latency. Graphs will be populated using a Brownian motion algorithm to ensure the lines look organic and 'noisy' rather than mathematically perfect.

ideas.name: TactileLab
ideas.niche: Precision mechanical keyboard switch performance profiling
ideas.problem: Keyboard enthusiasts rely on subjective reviews and single-point force measurements that fail to capture the nuanced tactile curves and bottom-out profiles required for high-end custom builds.
ideas.targetUser: Mechanical keyboard hobbyists, custom builders, and boutique switch manufacturers seeking empirical data to optimize typing feel and minimize expensive trial-and-error.
coreFeatures: Live Force-Displacement Graphing
Multi-Switch Profile Overlay
Automated Tactile Peak Detection
Community Signature Cloud Library
realDependencies: USB-HID or BLE Serial driver for load cell and encoder communication
High-frequency time-series database for telemetry storage
Advanced mathematical library for curve fitting and peak detection
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will simulate a hardware connection via a 3-second randomized 'Handshake' delay. Once 'connected', a mock stream will emit JSON packets every 10ms containing 'force_n' and 'travel_mm' values. To simulate different switches, the app will use pre-defined mathematical functions: a smooth quadratic curve for 'Linear' profiles and a function with an injected Gaussian spike for 'Tactile' profiles. These values will be fed into a mock WebSocket handler to drive the real-time UI graph.
